episodes.label: Shoulders of Giants — Nociceptor Ion Channels: Complement C5a/C3a, TRPV1, TRPM8 & Tetrodotoxin-Resistant Na+ Channels in Pain
episodes.notes: Five-Act biophysical journey from Bordet & Ehrlich's discovery of complement (1899), David Julius's cloning of TRPV1 (1997), Ardem Patapoutian's TRPM8 (2002), and Waxman/Wood's TTX-resistant nociceptor sodium channels (NaV1.8/NaV1.9) to collaborative studies revealing how C5a and C3a anaphylatoxins sensitize cutaneous heat and mechanical nociceptors via TRPV1 and NGF (Jang, Usachev, Brennan et al. 2010, Pain, PMC2814960), how natriuretic peptides vs IL-6 cytokines modulate cardiac nociceptive TRPV1 and TTXr-Na+ currents (Mohapatra, Usachev, Yorek MS 2011), and how corneal C-fiber TRPM8 osmosensing measures small-fiber integrity (PMC5113984).

episodes.label: Shoulders of Giants — Ion Channels & Gene Editing: NaV1.6 (SCN8A), Parvalbumin Interneuron Failure & Adenine Base Editing Rescue of Epilepsy
episodes.notes: Five-Act biophysical and genetic capstone tracing voltage-gated sodium channels from Hodgkin & Huxley (1952), Catterall's DIII-DIV IFM fast-inactivation latch, Raman & Bean's resurgent Na+ current (1997), Miriam Meisler's cloning of Scn8a (NaV1.6) and discovery of human SCN8A developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (2012), and Gaudelli & David Liu's invention of CRISPR Adenine Base Editors (2017) to recent brain-slice electrophysiology proving how gain-of-function SCN8A drives parvalbumin interneurons into premature depolarization block and synaptic failure (Miralles, Patel et al. 2024 JCI Insight, PMC11529981) and in vivo AAV adenine base editing rewriting R1872W back to wild-type to rescue seizures and sudden unexpected death in epilepsy (Reever, Meisler, Farber, Patel et al. 2026 JCI, PMC12871382).

episodes.label: The Days After the Bleed — Delayed Cerebral Ischemia After Aneurysmal SAH, Dihydropyridine Cav1.2 Fenestration Binding (PDB 5KMF / 8HMB), Pickard British Aneurysm Nimodipine Trial & Wrong-Route IV Boxed Warning

Six days after a ruptured aneurysm is secured, a woman who was speaking clearly can no longer name a key. The Critical Care Clinician follows her exam, arterial pressure and cerebral circulation. The Molecular Pharmacologist follows nimodipine from a Bayer patent into a membrane pocket, then asks which human outcomes changed. The case, values and dialogue are fictional. The Pharmacology notebook chapter “Voltage-Gated Calcium Channel Antagonists for the Central Nervous System” (2010) provides channel taxonomy through its Table 1 entry for CaV1.2/α1C. Primary studies supply the nimodipine evidence. Pharmacology notebook

episodes.label: The Diuretic That Tried to Quiet Seizures — Neonatal Electrographic-Only Seizures, Developmental NKCC1/KCC2 Chloride Shift (Rivera/Dzhala), Bumetanide NKCC1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9C0H) & NEMO/Soul Trials

episodes.label: The Burn That Came Before Relief — TRPV1 Cloning (Caterina 1997), Reversible Epidermal PGP 9.5 Nerve-Fiber Defunctionalization & 8% Capsaicin Patch Neuropathic Pain Trials
episodes.notes: From nociceptor channel cloning to reversible peripheral nerve-ending remodeling: Caterina et al.'s (1997) expression cloning of the heat- and capsaicin-gated cation channel TRPV1, Kennedy et al.'s (2010) serial skin-punch biopsies quantifying ~80% reversible PGP 9.5 epidermal nerve-fiber loss and 24-week regeneration after a 60-minute 8% capsaicin patch, and contrasting Backonja (2008, low-dose active control in PHN) vs. Bischoff (2014, inert placebo in post-herniorrhaphy pain) RCT outcomes.

episodes.label: The Rhythm That Changed Its Shape — Flecainide 1:1 Atrial Flutter & Use-Dependent QRS Widening, Cardiac Nav1.5 Pore Block (Jiang 2020) & The CAST Surrogate-Endpoint Paradox

episodes.label: Patch Clamping a Single Neuron
episodes.notes: Electrophysiological walkthrough of the 1980 gigaseal revolution and the biophysics of glass pipette fabrication using the Sutter P-1000. Details the technical transition from sharp electrodes to high-resistance seals, incorporating upright 40x water-immersion optics and precise pressure protocols for single-neuron recording at -70 mV.

episodes.label: Patch Clamping and Action Potential Biophysics
episodes.notes: Quantitative electrophysiological analysis of action potential kinetics using Clampfit 11.4 to derive Boltzmann conductance curves and phase-plane loops. Calculates the precise metabolic ATP cost of individual neuronal spikes while addressing technical artifacts such as NaV space-clamp escapes and P/N leak subtraction protocols.

episodes.label: Dehydrating in the Sub Angstrom Knock On of a Potassium Channel
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of the potassium channel selectivity filter, focusing on the sub-angstrom knock-on mechanism of ion conduction. Analyzes the femtometer-scale energetics of ion dehydration and the atomic-level coordination required for high-throughput permeability without sacrificing the strict exclusion of sodium ions.

episodes.label: How Living Cells Think With Electricity
episodes.notes: Mechanistic synthesis of the bioelectric dynasty, from Hodgkin and Huxley’s squid giant axon voltage clamps to Jens Christian Skou’s isolation of Na+/K+-ATPase from 25,000 shore crabs. Traces the evolution of patch-clamp electrophysiology through the KcsA selectivity filter and the 100-gigaohm resolution of single-channel molecular gating.

episodes.label: Patch Clamp Software versus Biophysical Reality
episodes.notes: Methodological audit of patch-clamp recording errors arising from uncompensated pipette capacitance, series resistance voltage drops, and liquid junction potentials. Critiques the digital interface of MultiClamp 700B and pCLAMP 11.4.1, emphasizing the biophysical necessity of bridge balance and RC low-pass filtering for accurate data acquisition.

episodes.label: The Channel That Quieted Insulin — Congenital Hyperinsulinism Critical Samples, Diazoxide KATP Opening, SUR1/Kir6.2 Comparator (PDB 7W4O), KCNJ11 Genetics & Pulmonary Hypertension

episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology of intrathecal ziconotide (PRIALT / omega-conotoxin MVIIA): Olivera's discovery of Conus magus peptide toxins, Nieng Yan's 3.1 Å cryo-EM structure of human CaV2.2 plugged by ziconotide (PDB 7MIX), why systemic IV delivery causes orthostatic hypotension via sympathetic CaV2.2 block while intrathecal delivery targets dorsal horn lamina I/II synapses without tolerance or respiratory depression, and Staats (2004) vs. Rauck (2006) titration kinetics.

episodes.label: The Drug That Changed the Ward — Chlorpromazine from Rhône-Poulenc Patent & 1952 Psychiatric Wards (Laborit, Delay & Elkes) to Pause-Triggered Torsades, Human hERG Cryo-EM (5VA1), DRD2 Kinetics & Sulfoxide LC-MS/MS
episodes.notes: Two ward records seventy years apart: chlorpromazine's transition from Rhône-Poulenc synthesis (US2645640A) and Laborit's 1952 surgical 'artificial hibernation' to Delay & Deniker's psychiatric cases, Elkes & Elkes's 1954 crossover, and the 1964 NIMH Collaborative Study, paired with a contemporary pause-triggered torsades workup (Fridericia QTc 531 ms), ligand-free human hERG cryo-EM (PDB 5VA1), oocyte vs. CHO IC50s (21.6 vs. 1.47 µM), and DRD2 residence kinetics.

episodes.label: One Ångström Through the Splenic Gate — Red Cell Interendothelial Slits, PIEZO1 Hereditary Xerocytosis (8YEZ/8YFG), Gardos KCNN4 & Ektacytometry
episodes.notes: Squeezing a human erythrocyte through a sub-micron splenic interendothelial slit: PIEZO1 mechanosensitive dome flattening and MDFIC-bound slowed inactivation (PDB 8YEZ/8YFG, 6.1 ms vs. 17.4 ms), Ca2+-activated Gardos (KCNN4) potassium/water efflux, osmotic gradient ektacytometry shifts, and why splenectomy triggers portal/thrombotic catastrophe in PIEZO1 hereditary xerocytosis.

episodes.label: One Ångström Riding the Flagellum — Sperm Capacitation, CatSper Pore Architecture (7EEB), Whole-Cell Patch Clamp & Hyperactivated Beat
episodes.notes: Atomic and electrophysiological journey along the principal piece of a sperm flagellum: mouse CatSperosome cryo-EM architecture (PDB 7EEB) vs. human cytoplasmic-droplet whole-cell patch-clamp recordings (Lishko/Strunker 2011; Mansell 2014), the 2016 ABHD2 hypothesis vs. 2026 selective inhibitor tests, and CATSPER-deficient IVF failure rescued by ICSI.

episodes.label: The Breath Before the Heat — Rising End-Tidal CO2 Before Hyperthermia, Skeletal Muscle RyR1 Calcium Leak, Dantrolene Channel Stabilization & Post-Crisis IVCT/CHCT vs. RYR1 Genetic Testing
episodes.notes: Intraoperative malignant hyperthermia from capnography to channel biophysics: why rising end-tidal carbon dioxide precedes core temperature elevation, uncontrolled skeletal muscle ryanodine receptor (RyR1) sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium release, dantrolene sodium stabilization of RyR1, and post-crisis workup integrating RYR1 variant sequencing with caffeine-halothane contracture testing.

episodes.label: The Rhythm the Drug Could Break — Dofetilide (Tikosyn) Inpatient QT Gate, Human hERG Cryo-EM Cavity (PDB 5VA2), Reverse Use-Dependence, Renal OCT2/MATE1 & the DIAMOND Trials
episodes.notes: Biophysics, structural biology, and clinical safety engineering of dofetilide (Tikosyn): Sanguinetti's IKr/hERG discovery, Wang & MacKinnon's human Kv11.1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 5VA2) and Tyr652/Phe656 drug-trapping cavity, reverse use-dependence at slow sinus rates after cardioversion, renal OCT2/MATE1 transport interactions, and the DIAMOND trials.

episodes.label: The Channel That Wouldn't Let Calcium Through — Extended-Release Verapamil Overdose, Fleckenstein's Calcium Antagonism, Rabbit CaV1.1 Cryo-EM (6JPA), Beta-Cell Hyperglycemia & High-Dose Insulin Therapy
episodes.notes: From Albrecht Fleckenstein's discovery of calcium antagonism to critical-care toxicology: rabbit CaV1.1 cryo-EM structure bound to (S)-verapamil in two central-cavity poses (PDB 6JPA), AV-nodal conduction block, pancreatic beta-cell L-type channel blockade producing diagnostic hyperglycemia, stereoselective CYP3A4 clearance, high-dose insulin euglycemia therapy, and EXTRIP non-dialyzability.

episodes.label: The Rhythm That Waited for the Treadmill — CPVT Exercise Stress ECG (H042), Post-Exertional Bidirectional VT, RYR2 Diastolic Calcium Leak & Paired-Test Repeatability
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H042) investigation of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT): why resting ECGs and structural echocardiography are normal, how adrenergic surge and early post-exercise recovery unmask beat-to-beat alternating bidirectional ventricular tachycardia (Akiba et al. 2026), RYR2 diastolic Ca2+ leak and NCX1 delayed afterdepolarizations (Steinberg et al. 2023), and exercise-test repeatability limits (Peltenburg et al. 2023).

episodes.label: Why a Visual Signal Can Arrive Late After Sight Improves — Dawson's 1954 Signal Averaging, Halliday's 1972 Pattern-Reversal VEP in Optic Neuritis & Sokol's Dioptric Blur Artifact
episodes.notes: Clinical neurophysiology of pattern-reversal Visual Evoked Potentials (VEP): Dawson's (1954) time-locked signal averaging, Halliday, McDonald & Mushin's (1972) discovery of persistent monocular cortical latency delay after visual acuity recovery in optic neuritis, and Sokol & Moskowitz's (1981) demonstration of refractive blur latency artifacts.

episodes.label: How a Nerve Test Finds Where a Signal Slows — Helmholtz's 1850 Two-Point Subtraction, Hodes's 1948 Human CMAP Velocity, Simpson/Gilliatt Focal Wrist Latency & Ring-Finger Comparison
episodes.notes: Electrophysiology of clinical nerve conduction studies (H045): Helmholtz's (1850) two-point latency subtraction canceling synaptic and contractile delay, Hodes, Larrabee & German's (1948) percutaneous human compound muscle action potential (CMAP) conduction velocity method, Simpson (1956) and Gilliatt & Sears's (1958) localization of focal median nerve entrapment across the carpal tunnel, and Uncini et al.'s (1989) ring-finger median-vs-ulnar internal control.

episodes.label: Why a Fly's Eye Went Quiet in the Light — Cosens & Manning's 1969 Drosophila trp Mutant, Montell's Gene Rescue, Hardie & Minke's Ca2+-Selective Current, Niemeyer's trp/trpl Double Mutant & Asp621 Pore Selectivity
episodes.notes: Discovery of the founding TRP ion channel in Drosophila vision: Cosens & Manning's (1969) transient receptor potential mutant fading in continuous light, Montell & Rubin's gene rescue and cloning, Hardie & Minke's (1992) single-photoreceptor patch-clamp proof of missing Ca2+ permeability, Niemeyer et al.'s (1996) trp/trpl dissection, and Liu et al.'s (2007) pore-selectivity mutagenesis.

episodes.label: How You Know Where Your Hand Is in the Dark — Goodwin's 100 Hz Tendon-Vibration Illusion, Ghez's Multi-Joint Reaching Without Proprioception, Woo's Piezo2 Spindles & Chesler's Human PIEZO2 Loss
episodes.notes: From psychophysical illusions to the molecular mechanosensor of proprioception: Goodwin, McCloskey & Matthews (1972) tendon-vibration muscle-spindle illusions, Ghez et al. (1995) intersegmental dynamics defects in deafferented human reaching rescued partially by vision, Woo et al. (2015) conditional Piezo2 ablation silencing muscle-spindle Ia afferents, and Chesler et al. (2016) human PIEZO2 deficiency.

episodes.label: How Scientists Followed Carbon Through a Tumor — Warburg's 1927 Artery-Vein Lactate Balance, DeBerardinis's 13C NMR Glioblastoma TCA & Glutaminolysis & Hensley's Intraoperative Lung Tumor Infusions
episodes.notes: From the classical Warburg Effect to human intraoperative stable-isotope tracing: Warburg, Wind & Negelein (1927) aerobic glycolysis across rat tumor vessels, DeBerardinis et al. (2007) 13C NMR isotopomer resolution of simultaneous glycolysis, TCA flux, fatty acid synthesis, and glutamine anaplerosis in glioblastoma cells, and Hensley et al. (2016) intraoperative [U-13C]glucose infusions in human NSCLC patients.

episodes.label: A Sodium Channel for Pain and Smell — Cox's SCN9A (NaV1.7) Nonsense Variants, Patch-Clamp Loss of Current & Weiss's Olfactory Glomerular Synaptic Failure
episodes.notes: How one voltage-gated sodium channel links nociception and olfaction: Cox et al. (2006) biallelic SCN9A (NaV1.7) truncations eliminating pain while sparing touch, and Weiss et al. (2011) dual recordings proving NaV1.7-null olfactory sensory neurons fire odor-evoked action potentials at the soma but fail to trigger synaptic transmission in the olfactory bulb glomerulus.

episodes.label: The Glucose That Couldn't Leave the Liver — Glycogen Storage Disease Type Ia, ER G6PC1 His176 Phosphohistidine Catalysis vs. SLC37A4, Uncooked Cornstarch & DTX401 Gene Therapy
episodes.notes: From acute fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis in glycogen storage disease type Ia to ER lumenal G6PC1 His176 phosphohistidine hydrolysis vs. SLC37A4 glucose-6-phosphate transport, Grefhorst's ChREBP/LXRalpha mouse blockade vs. human [6,6-2H2]glucose flux, uncooked cornstarch therapy, and AAV8 G6PC1 gene replacement.

episodes.label: The Sugar That Stayed After the Milk Was Gone — Classic Galactosemia, GALT Ping-Pong His186 Catalysis (5IN3), Endogenous [1-13C]Galactose Production & Aldose Reductase
episodes.notes: Why lifelong dietary galactose restriction saves neonates from acute hepatorenal crisis yet fails to prevent long-term speech and ovarian complications in classic galactosemia: human GALT double-displacement His186 uridylylation (PDB 5IN3), Berry et al. [1-13C]galactose isotope-dilution proof of ~1 g/day endogenous galactose synthesis, and aldose reductase galactitol reduction.

episodes.label: The Hormone That Heard Less Protein — Dietary Protein Restriction, Hepatocyte FGF21 Induction, Beta-Klotho 5VAQ Docking, FAP Cleavage & Intact vs. Total ELISA
episodes.notes: Endocrine and structural dissection of human FGF21 induction during low-protein and sucrose feeding (Nicolaisen, Ramne, Laeger): C-terminal beta-Klotho docking (PDB 5VAQ), fibroblast activation protein (FAP) Pro171 cleavage separating intact bioactive FGF21 from total immunoreactive FGF21, and central Klb macronutrient preference circuits.

episodes.label: The Leucine That Wouldn’t Clear — Maple Syrup Urine Disease, BCKDH E1 Phosphorylation (1DTW/1OLS), Isobaric LC-MS/MS Alloisoleucine & Liver Transplant Flux
episodes.notes: Biochemical and analytical dissection of Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD) decompensation: human BCKDH E1 alpha-ketoacid decarboxylation and BCKDK Ser292 phosphorylation (PDB 1DTW/1OLS/4H7Q), chromatographic separation of isobaric leucine, isoleucine, alloisoleucine, and hydroxyproline at m/z 132->86, LAT1 blood-brain barrier competition, IV BCAA-free rescue, and liver transplantation.

episodes.label: The First Calories Back — Refeeding Syndrome, Insulin-Driven Phosphate/Potassium Shifts, PDH E1 ThDP Geometry (1NI4) & Doig ICU Trial
episodes.notes: From starvation to refeeding syndrome in the ICU: insulin-stimulated Na+/K+-ATPase potassium uptake and intracellular phosphate trapping, human pyruvate dehydrogenase E1 thiamine diphosphate (ThDP) active-site geometry (PDB 1NI4), whole-blood ThDP LC-MS/MS assays, diaphragmatic weakness in hypophosphatemia (Aubier 1985), and the Doig et al. (2015) caloric restriction trial.

episodes.label: What the Colon Sends Back — Inulin Fermentation, Eudragit Colon-Targeted [1-13C]SCFAs, Systemic Availability (36% Acetate, 9% Propionate, 2% Butyrate) & FFAR2 8J24
episodes.notes: Atomic and clinical tracing of colonic short-chain fatty acids (Boets et al. 2015, 2017; Bloemen et al. 2009): Bacteroides ovatus inulin cleavage, Roseburia/Faecalibacterium acetate-to-butyrate cross-feeding, Eudragit S100 colon-targeted [1-13C]SCFA capsules with IV [2H]SCFA clearance calibration (36% acetate, 9.2% propionate, 2.4% butyrate systemic availability), and human FFAR2 cryo-EM (PDB 8J24).

episodes.label: Three Roads to Liver Fat — Chylomicron NEFA Spillover, Multi-Tracer Liver Biopsies, Human FASN 9MJ9 & Beverage De Novo Lipogenesis
episodes.notes: Quantitative isotope dissection of hepatic triacylglycerol sources across three human studies: Piché et al. (2018) chylomicron-derived [U-13C]palmitate spillover, Donnelly et al. (2005) 4-day triple-tracer liver biopsies (59% NEFA, 26% DNL, 15% dietary within accounted fraction), human FASN cryo-EM (PDB 9MJ9), and Geidl-Flueck et al. (2021) sugar-sweetened beverage VLDL-palmitate secretion.

episodes.notes: Stable-isotope tracing of ingested [U-13C6]fructose in humans (Theytaz et al. 2014): GLUT5 uptake, ketohexokinase KHK-A vs. KHK-C phosphorylation (PDB 2HW1), aldolase B cleavage, GC-C-IRMS 13C-glucose and breath 13CO2 recovery, paired with 7-Tesla hepatic deuterium metabolic imaging (Brunasso et al. 2026).

episodes.notes: Atomic-to-clinical journey through mucociliary clearance and Primary Ciliary Dyskinesia (PCD): human airway doublet microtubule structure (Walton et al. 2023, PDB 8J07), periciliary brush osmotic exclusion (Button et al. 2012), nasal nitric oxide chemiluminescence, and DNAH5 intronic splice-site RT-PCR.

episodes.notes: Atomic and clinical timeline of the first minutes after coronary artery reperfusion: Jennings & Reimer's (1960/1977) canine wavefront of necrosis, coronary-sinus succinate release, Complex I flavin site reverse electron transport (RET) superoxide burst upon reoxygenation, and why ischemic postconditioning failed to reduce clinical STEMI endpoints.

episodes.label: One Ångström Across the Gut Barrier — Enteric Translocation, TLR4–MD-2 Lipid A Dimerization (3FXI), Microvascular Shunting & Septic Shock
episodes.notes: From an injured intestinal barrier and mesenteric lymph node cultures (Deitch 1989) to the crystal structure of human TLR4-MD-2 bound to E. coli Ra LPS (PDB 3FXI), sublingual microvascular shunting (De Backer 2002), endothelial glycocalyx shedding, and why eritoran MD-2 blockade failed in the Phase III ACCESS sepsis trial.

episodes.label: One Ångström from a Dividing Cell — Paclitaxel in the β-Tubulin Taxane Pocket (1JFF), Cremophor Anaphylaxis & Mitotic Spindle Fate
episodes.notes: Atomic-scale journey into the luminal beta-tubulin taxane pocket (PDB 1JFF): distinguishing Cremophor EL complement-mediated infusion anaphylaxis from delayed neutropenia, M-loop lateral protofilament stabilization, and multipolar mitotic spindle catastrophe in human tumors.

episodes.label: How the End of a Pathway Slows the Beginning — Yates & Pardee's Pyrimidine Feedback, Gerhart & Schachman's Dissociated Catalytic vs. Regulatory ATCase Subunits & the 1965 MWC Allosteric Model
episodes.notes: Birth of molecular allostery: from Yates & Pardee's (1956) pyrimidine end-product inhibition in E. coli to Gerhart & Pardee's (1962) heat-desensitized aspartate transcarbamoylase (ATCase), Gerhart & Schachman's (1965) separation and reassembly of catalytic and regulatory subunits, and the Monod-Wyman-Changeux (1965) conformational equilibrium model.

episodes.label: How Scientists Saw ATP Synthase Turn — Abrahams & Walker's Asymmetric F1 Crystal States, Noji & Yoshida's Spinning Actin Filament (120° Steps) & Itoh's Magnetic-Bead Mechanical ATP Synthesis
episodes.notes: Direct proof of rotary catalysis in F1-ATPase: Abrahams et al. (1994) 2.8 Å crystal snapshot of three distinct catalytic β conformations around an asymmetric γ axle, Noji et al. (1997) single-molecule fluorescence microscopy of unidirectional counterclockwise γ rotation and Yasuda et al. (1998) discrete 120° steps, and Itoh et al. (2004) electromagnet-driven clockwise rotation forcing net ATP synthesis.

episodes.label: How a Cell Pumps Ions Uphill — Skou's 1957 Crab-Nerve Na++K+-Synergistic ATPase, Post's Phosphoenzyme Intermediate, Garrahan & Glynn's 3 Na+:2 K+:1 ATP Stoichiometry & Goldin's Inside-Out Vesicles
episodes.notes: Enzymology and vectorial reconstitution of the sodium-potassium pump: Skou (1957) discovery of the Mg2+/Na+/K+-activated ATPase in Carcinus maenas nerve membranes, Post, Sen & Rosenthal (1965) acyl-phosphate intermediate formed with Na+ and hydrolyzed with K+, Garrahan & Glynn (1967) 3 Na+ : 2 K+ : 1 ATP coupling ratio in resealed red-cell ghosts, and Goldin (1977) inside-out liposome reconstitution.

episodes.label: How a Cell Senses Low Oxygen — Semenza's EPO 3' Enhancer & HIF-1α/β Purification, Maxwell's VHL Ubiquitin-Tagged Normoxic Degradation & Ivan/Jaakkola's Pro564 Oxygen-Dependent Hydroxylation
episodes.notes: Molecular mechanism of cellular oxygen sensing: Semenza et al. (1991) & Wang et al. (1995) identification of the hypoxia-response element and HIF-1α/ARNT heterodimer, Maxwell et al. (1999) proof that pVHL targets HIF-α for oxygen-dependent ubiquitylation and proteasomal destruction, and Ivan et al. (2001) & Jaakkola et al. (2001) discovery of enzymatic Pro564 4-hydroxylation as the direct oxygen switch.

episodes.label: How a Potassium Channel Chooses an Ion — Bezanilla & Armstrong's Squid Axon Na+ Block, Heginbotham's TVGYG Signature Mutations & Doyle & MacKinnon's KcsA Selectivity Filter
episodes.notes: Atomic solution to the potassium channel selectivity paradox: Bezanilla & Armstrong (1972) >10:1 K+/Na+ selectivity and internal Na+ block in perfused squid axons, Heginbotham et al. (1994) TVGYG pore-loop mutagenesis converting a K+-selective pore into a nonselective cation channel, Doyle et al. (1998) & Zhou et al. (2001) 2.0 Å KcsA crystal structures showing backbone carbonyl cages matching dehydrated K+, and Thompson et al. (2009) planar Na+ binding.

episodes.label: How a Cell Builds a Droplet in the Right Place — C. elegans P Granules, Brangwynne's Shear-Induced Dripping & FRAP Recovery, MEX-5 Gradient Dissolution & MEG-3 Scaffolding
episodes.notes: Discovery of intracellular liquid-liquid phase separation: Hird et al. (1996) live GFP::PIE-1 imaging of C. elegans P granules, Brangwynne et al. (2009) proof of liquid wetting, fusion, ~second FRAP exchange, and spatial condensation/dissolution asymmetry, and Smith et al. (2016) & Folkmann et al. (2021) MEX-5 RNA competition and intrinsically disordered MEG-3 surface clusters.

episodes.label: Mitochondrial Cristae Protons and Calcium Storms
episodes.notes: Biophysical resolution of the mitochondrial cristae vault as a high-voltage proton capacitor and its catastrophic failure during calcium-mediated pore transition. Analyzes the 1-Ångström structural dynamics of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP) alongside the bioenergetic collapse driving regulated cell death.

episodes.label: Riding an Olive Oil Lipid Into a Chylomicron
episodes.notes: Surfing the S-N-2 olive-oil lipid involves pancreatic colipase lid-flip mechanics, micellar emulsification, and intracellular re-esterification into nascent chylomicrons. This atomic biophysics analysis contrasts Ernest Overton's 1899 lipid sieve tables with modern cryo-EM membrane transporter structures.

episodes.label: Tracking Ethanol From First Sip to Exhalation
episodes.notes: Pharmacokinetic and biophysical dissection of ethanol absorption, distribution, and elimination pathways from initial ingestion to alveolar exhalation. Examines TRPV1 receptor activation on the lingual epithelium alongside 4.5-angstrom molecular models of alcohol distribution across biological barriers.

episodes.label: One Angstrom Hearing and Dancing Cochlear Hair Cells
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of cochlear hair cell mechanotransduction at the 1-Angstrom scale, focusing on tip-link tension and Prestin-mediated electromotility at 20 kilohertz. Integrates the molecular mechanisms of cisplatin-induced ototoxicity and ROS-driven mitochondrial injury within the auditory sensory apparatus.

episodes.label: Hemoglobin Sub Angstrom Iron Snap and Sickle Fibers
episodes.notes: Structural and biophysical resolution of the four-tenths of an Angstrom iron snap within the hemoglobin tetramer during oxygenation. Traces the allosteric transitions involving Bohr protons and the polymerization kinetics of sickle rods, integrating the historical contributions of Max Perutz and Takuo Aoyagi to atomic-scale physiology.

episodes.label: How Kidneys Filter and Rescue 180 Liters Daily
episodes.notes: Biophysical and molecular resolution of renal glucose reclamation and glomerular filtration barriers. Analyzes the 1-Ångström structural mechanics of nephrin slit zippers alongside SGLT2 and GLUT1 transport kinetics that facilitate the daily recovery of 180 grams of D-glucose from 180 liters of ultrafiltrate.

episodes.label: How Immune Cells Invent New DNA From Scratch
episodes.notes: Molecular and biophysical resolution of V(D)J recombination, focusing on RAG1/2-mediated chromosomal cleavage and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase activity in T-cell receptor assembly. Connects these mechanisms of de novo DNA synthesis to clinical diagnostic challenges in identifying Babesia parasites through whole-blood PCR and catch-bond kinetics.

episodes.label: Crawling Through the Glycocalyx Jungle to the Endothelial Gate
episodes.notes: Biophysical investigation of endothelial surface layer barrier mechanics and vascular permeability. Analyzes endothelial glycocalyx structure, hydrodynamic shear stress sensing, catch-bond kinetics, and integrin mechanotransduction.

episodes.label: Escorting One Actinium Atom From Birth to a Tumor
episodes.notes: Atomic and pharmacokinetic tracking of Actinium-225 from its cyclotronic origin to its targeted deposition within the tumor cell nucleus. Examines the precision biophysics of radioligand chelation and the 1-Ångström molecular machinery required to deliver high-LET alpha radiation while sparing adjacent healthy parenchyma.

episodes.label: Hanging from AKAP1 Over the Abyss of Fission
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of the AKAP1 mitochondrial firewall and its regulatory role in preventing catastrophic organelle fission. Examines the 1-Ångström molecular machinery governing mitochondrial dynamics, focusing on how AKAP1 scaffolds protein kinase A to modulate the metabolic response to oxidative stress injury.

episodes.label: Confessions of a Peroxidized Lipid in Status Epilepticus
episodes.notes: Biophysical reconstruction of ferroptotic membrane failure and lipid peroxidation during refractory status epilepticus. Traces the cascade from NMDA receptor-mediated excitotoxicity to the catastrophic collapse of neuronal membrane integrity, linking oxidative stress to the irreversible metabolic failure seen in clinical coma.

episodes.label: Assembly Unfurling and Lysis by the Complement MAC
episodes.notes: Structural and biophysical resolution of the 100-angstrom complement membrane attack complex, tracing C5b-9 polymerization and transmembrane pore formation. Analyzes the molecular machinery of targeted cellular lysis, immunopathology, and cell-membrane disruption.

episodes.label: Tug of War Along the Microtubule Highway in Motor Neurons
episodes.notes: Biophysical resolution of dual-motor mechanics and axonal deadlock within the microtubule transport system of motor neurons. Analyzes the 1-Angstrom cryo-EM structural dynamics of dynein and kinesin interactions that govern allosteric regulation and prevent metabolic collapse during mitochondrial stress or hypoxic injury.

episodes.label: Inside the Stomach Two Million Fold Acid Forge
episodes.notes: Structural and thermodynamic resolution of the gastric parietal canaliculus as a biological acid forge capable of maintaining a 2.5-million-fold proton gradient. Examines the H+/K+-ATPase molecular machinery at 1-Ångström resolution to explain the bioenergetic cost and ion-pumping precision required for human digestive acidification.

episodes.label: Riding a Newborn Neutrophil to Bleach and NETosis
episodes.notes: Immunopathological and biophysical reconstruction of the 12-hour lifespan of a neutrophil, from initial activation to the oxidative burst and NETosis. Analyzes the molecular mechanisms of hypochlorous acid production and the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps as a terminal defense strategy against sepsis and inflammatory crises.

episodes.label: How One Photon Snaps Retinal in 200 Femtoseconds
episodes.notes: Ultrafast biophysical analysis of rhodopsin photoactivation, detailing the two hundred femtosecond isomerization of 11-cis-retinal and subsequent conformational changes transduced across visual pigment protein structures.

episodes.label: Jumping the Neuromuscular Synapse to Myosin Rigor
episodes.notes: Structural and electrophysiological resolution of the neuromuscular junction, examining SNARE complex zippering, acetylcholinesterase inhibition, and myosin rigor mortis. Details the atomic-scale molecular mechanisms governing synaptic vesicle exocytosis and irreversible skeletal muscle contraction arrest.

episodes.label: Crossing the Blood Brain Barrier and Glutamate Elevators
episodes.notes: Biophysical investigation of blood-brain barrier transport mechanics and astrocytic regulation. Analyzes GLUT1 glucose transport, the 18-angstrom EAAT2 glutamate elevator, and lactate shuttling kinetics across cerebral endothelial tight junctions.

episodes.label: Melting Through Nuclear Pores Into the Ribosome Tunnel
episodes.notes: Atomic-scale investigation of macromolecular transport through the nuclear pore complex’s phenylalanine-glycine hydrogel and the subsequent entry into the 80S ribosome birth canal. Utilizes 1-Ångström cryo-EM structural data to map the biophysical trajectory of nascent polypeptides as they navigate the ribosomal tunnel during protein synthesis.

episodes.label: How Blood Shear Unspools Clotting Strings in Arteries
episodes.notes: Mechanistic biophysics of high-shear vascular thrombosis and hemostatic plug formation. Explores von Willebrand factor unspooling under extreme fluid shear stress alongside TMEM16F channel activation and fibrin network polymerization.

episodes.label: The Breakfast That Changed a Bargain — Controlled 850-kcal Breakfast Crossovers in Ultimatum Bargaining (Strang 2017) vs. fMRI Risk Lotteries (Liu 2021), Plasma Tyrosine/LNAA & Human Tyrosine Hydroxylase Cryo-EM (6ZZU/6ZVP)
episodes.notes: How acute macronutrient swaps in controlled 850-kcal breakfasts affect distinct economic decision tasks: Strang et al.'s (2017) Ultimatum Game crossover (unfair-offer rejection and plasma tyrosine/LNAA AUC) vs. Liu et al.'s (2021) fMRI monetary lottery crossover (overall behavioral null, fat-mass interaction, tryptophan/LNAA correlation, and parietal BOLD thresholds), grounded in human tyrosine hydroxylase cryo-EM structures (PDB 6ZZU apo & 6ZVP dopamine-bound).

episodes.label: The Fat That Stayed in the Bone — Paradoxical Bone Marrow Adiposity in Anorexia Nervosa, 3T L4 vs. Femoral PRESS 1H-MRS, Marrow Adiponectin & Human ADIPOR2 Crystal (5LX9), 12-Month Epiphyseal Divergence & P1NP/β-CTX
episodes.notes: Why vertebral bone marrow fat rises during peripheral fat depletion in anorexia nervosa: Bredella's 3T PRESS 1H-MRS lipid/water ratios vs. areal DXA Z-scores, Cawthorn's Ocn-Wnt10b mouse calorie-restriction adiponectin experiments and human ADIPOR2 zinc-ceramidase structure (PDB 5LX9), Fazeli's 12-month longitudinal surprise (+25.3% femoral epiphyseal marrow fat alongside rising lumbar BMD), and P1NP/beta-CTX/LSC clinical boundaries.

episodes.label: The Amino Acid at the Brain's Gate — Six-Competitor Plasma Tryptophan Ratio, Human LAT1 Cryo-EM (8J8M/8XPU), TPH2 & PET Tracer Assumptions, Delgado's Remission Relapse Trials (14/21; 8/15 vs. 1/15) & Breakfast Limits
episodes.notes: From plasma amino-acid competition at blood-brain barrier LAT1–CD98hc (PDB 8J8M L-Trp & 8XPU JPH203) to acute tryptophan depletion trials: UHPLC-MS/MS separation of isobaric Leu/Ile, recombinant TPH2 kinetics vs. alpha-[11C]methyl-L-Trp PET assumptions, Delgado's remitted depression crossover (14/21) and SSRI vs. desipramine responder split (8/15 vs. 1/15), and why Wurtman's breakfast study measured plasma ratios rather than mood.

episodes.label: What the Sugar Test Sees — Pediatric Growth Faltering, Claudin-15 Pore Architecture (4P79), Lactulose:Rhamnose Concentration (0.50) vs. Recovery Ratio (0.10), EED Biopsy Morphometry & MAL-ED / WASH Benefits
episodes.notes: Deconstructing dual-sugar intestinal permeability testing in pediatric growth faltering and environmental enteric dysfunction (EED): mouse claudin-15 crystal coordinates (PDB 4P79) vs. neutral sugar probes, why identical 30-90 minute urine bags yield 0.50 by concentration vs. 0.10 by fractional dose recovery on LC-MS/MS, EEDBI duodenal villus morphometry (n=96), MAL-ED (n=1,469), and WASH Benefits Bangladesh (n=4,584).

episodes.label: The Bowel That Learned to Absorb Again — Short-Bowel High-Output Jejunostomy Secretory Losses, GLP-2R Cryo-EM & Teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 Shielding & STEPS Parenteral Weaning
episodes.notes: Intestinal rehabilitation in short-bowel syndrome with end-jejunostomy: net secretory stoma sodium/water balance vs. renal sodium conservation, colonic salvage anatomy, human GLP-2–GLP-2R–Gs cryo-EM structure and teduglutide Ala2→Gly2 DPP-4 resistance, villus height/crypt depth trophic remodeling, and Jeppesen's STEPS randomized parenteral-support reduction trial.

episodes.label: The Colon Cancer Signal in the Diet Survey — Fecal Immunochemical Screening Conversion, MGMT Cys145 Suicide Alkyl Transfer, Le Leu's Red-Meat vs. Butyrylated-Starch Rectal Crypt Biopsies & UK Biobank GxE
episodes.notes: Separating stool hemoglobin screening, mucosal adduct biology, and observational nutritional epidemiology: FIT buffer-to-feces (µg Hb/g) conversion, human MGMT Cys145 suicidal O6-methylguanine repair (PDB 1EH6/1T38), Le Leu et al. (2015) randomized high-red-meat ± butyrylated resistant starch rectal biopsy O6MeG adduct trial, and gene-by-diet interaction studies.

episodes.label: When the Brain Burns Ketones — Drug-Resistant Pediatric Epilepsy, SCOT Succinyl-CoA Transferase (3DLX / 1OOY), [11C]Acetoacetate PET, Decanoate AMPA Block & the Neal Trial
episodes.notes: From the 4:1 ketogenic diet ratio (90% energy from fat) and hepatic HMGCS2 ketogenesis to extrahepatic SCOT/OXCT1 glutamyl-CoA thioester catalysis (human apo PDB 3DLX vs. porcine Glu305 intermediate PDB 1OOY), dual [11C]acetoacetate/[18F]FDG brain PET, Chang et al. (2016) decanoic acid GluA2/GluA3 AMPA receptor antagonism, and Neal et al.'s (2008) randomized childhood epilepsy trial (145 randomized, 103 analyzed at 3 months).

episodes.label: The Ammonia That Had Nowhere to Go — Postpartum Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) Crisis, PALO vs. Carbamoyl-Phosphate 1OTH/1FVO Structures, Urine Orotate LC-MS/MS & Nitrogen Scavengers
episodes.notes: Postpartum hyperammonemic decompensation in heterozygous Ornithine Transcarbamylase (OTC) deficiency (Arn et al. 1990): pre-analytical ammonia release in warm whole blood, human OTC domain closure around PALO vs. carbamoyl phosphate + norvaline (PDB 1OTH, 1FVO), mitochondrial carbamoyl-phosphate spillover into CAD-driven urinary orotate (m/z 155->111), and phenylacetate/benzoate nitrogen scavenging.

episodes.label: The Allele at the Mediterranean Table — TCF7L2 rs7903146 Islet Chromatin Accessibility, Beta-Catenin 1JPW Interface, PREDIMED Stroke Subgroup & the 2018 Trial Reanalysis
episodes.notes: From intronic TCF7L2 rs7903146 C-to-T open chromatin in human pancreatic islets (Gaulton et al. 2010) and beta-catenin groove binding (PDB 1JPW) to Corella et al.'s (2013) PREDIMED genotype-stratified stroke analysis (n=7,018 / 4,727) and Estruch et al.'s (2018) NEJM retraction-republication accounting for household and clinic non-randomization.

episodes.notes: From PREDICT 1 (Berry et al. 2020, n=1,002) inter-individual postprandial glucose and triglyceride variability to glucose oxidase FAD electrochemistry (PDB 1CF3), simultaneous same-brand vs. cross-brand CGM meal ranking discordance (Merino 2022; Hengist 2025 inpatient duplicate meals), and the Personal Diet Study vs. METHOD randomized trials.

episodes.notes: Reconciling the University of Wisconsin (2009, 2014) and NIA (2012, 2017) rhesus macaque caloric restriction colonies: age at onset, purified 28.5% sucrose ad libitum controls vs. natural-ingredient rationed controls, age-related vs. all-cause Cox hazard ratios, human Sestrin2 leucine-pocket structure (PDB 5DJ4), and the human 2-year CALERIE trial.

episodes.label: The Bile Acid That Missed the Return Trip — Ileal ASBT Reclamation, FXR–FGF19–CYP7A1 Feedback (6HL1), 75SeHCAT Retention, Serum C4 & SINBAD Trial
episodes.notes: Enterohepatic circulation and bile acid malabsorption: apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter (ASBT/SLC10A2), human FXR ligand-binding domain (PDB 6HL1), ileal FGF19 suppression of hepatic CYP7A1, 7-day 75SeHCAT gamma retention vs. fasting serum 7alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4), and colesevelam sequestration in the SINBAD trial.

episodes.label: The Antibody and the Unhealed Colon — Infliximab TNF-Alpha Trimer Crystal Structure (PDB 4G3Y), Transmembrane Avidity, Endoscopic Mucosal Healing (ACT 1/2) & Anti-Drug Antibody Clearance
episodes.notes: Structural immunology and therapeutic drug monitoring of infliximab in ulcerative colitis: chimeric cA2 engineering (Knight 1993), 2.60 Å TNF-alpha:infliximab Fab crystal structure (PDB 4G3Y, Liang 2013), transmembrane TNF bivalent avidity (Scallon 2002), ACT 1 & ACT 2 mucosal healing trials (Rutgeerts 2005), and anti-drug antibody clearance vs. assay non-interchangeability.

episodes.label: The Sedative You Can Wake From — Dexmedetomidine Locus Coeruleus Alpha-2A Cryo-EM, GIRK Hyperpolarization, Vascular vs. Sympatholytic Biphasic Pressure & SPICE III / MENDS2 Trials
episodes.notes: Molecular and critical-care pharmacology of dexmedetomidine: chiral resolution of medetomidine into its active S/d-enantiomer (1990), locus coeruleus alpha-2A Gi/o-GIRK hyperpolarization and sleep-pathway disinhibition vs. GABA-A coma, human alpha-2A cryo-EM binding pocket geometry, biphasic peripheral alpha-2B vasoconstriction vs. central sympatholysis, and the MENDS, MIDEX/PRODEX, SPICE III, and MENDS2 clinical trials.

episodes.label: What the Hair Could Tell Us — Early Iron Age Tunnug 1 Cannabis Burial, Hair-Shaft CBN LC-HRMS/MS vs. Environmental Transfer, Human CB1-Gi1 Cryo-EM (PDB 9ERX) & Hallstatt Radiocarbon
episodes.notes: Archaeotoxicology and receptor pharmacology of ancient cannabis at Tunnug 1 (Tuva, Early Iron Age): LC-HRMS/MS detection of cannabinol (CBN) in a preserved human hair braid alongside 965 botanical cannabis seeds, Hallstatt Plateau 14C calibration, human CB1-Gi1 cryo-EM structure (PDB 9ERX), forensic hair-testing boundaries between smoke/handling transfer and metabolic THC-COOH incorporation (Moosmann et al. 2015), and comparative Eurasian archaeobotany.

episodes.label: The Sedative the Screen Missed — GABAA alpha1-beta2-gamma2 Cryo-EM Allosteric Binding (6X3X/6X3U), Diazepam CYP2C19/3A4 vs. Lorazepam Direct UGT2B15 Glucuronidation & Why Urine Immunoassays Miss Lorazepam-Glucuronide
episodes.notes: Receptor allostery, metabolic routing, and toxicology screen blind spots: cryo-EM structures of human alpha1-beta2-gamma2 GABAA receptors bound to diazepam (PDB 6X3X) and flumazenil (PDB 6X3U), Sternbach's benzodiazepine chemistry, diazepam CYP oxidation vs. lorazepam direct C3-OH glucuronidation, and why unhydrolyzed urine benzodiazepine immunoassays miss lorazepam-glucuronide without beta-glucuronidase hydrolysis and LC-MS/MS.

episodes.label: The Switch That Keeps Us Awake — Hypothalamic Orexin/Hypocretin Discovery, Canine HCRTR2 & Human CSF Orexin-A Deficiency in Narcolepsy Type 1, OX2R Crystal Structures (4S0V/7L1U) & Dual Orexin Receptor Antagonists
episodes.notes: From wake-maintenance physiology to targeted insomnia pharmacology: 1998 discovery of hypothalamic hypocretins/orexins, 1999 canine HCRTR2 and murine knockout narcolepsy models, human CSF orexin-A <=110 pg/mL cutoff in ICSD-3 narcolepsy type 1, structural comparison of antagonist-bound (PDB 4S0V) vs. agonist-bound (PDB 7L1U) OX2R, and clinical trials and next-morning safety of suvorexant and daridorexant.

episodes.notes: Clinical Cluster & Cardiopulmonary Physiology synthesis of ambulatory ECG monitoring (H041), cardiac exercise stress testing (H042), and lung volumes/DLCO (H043): Barrett's paired patch cohort (n=146), EMBRACE (n=572) & CRYSTAL AF (n=441), nocturnal vagal variants, and toothbrush pseudo-VT; coronary autoregulation, ST localization laws, LBBB vasodilator rule, Cole's HRR (n=2,428), WOMEN & ISCHEMIA; and Boyle's Law plethysmography vs. gas dilution, Roughton-Forster DLCO/KCO physics, CPFE/PAH phenotypes, ppo-DLCO, and race-neutral GLI Z-scores.

episodes.label: The Drug That Took the Long Way — Parkinson's Vallecular Tablet Retention on Videofluoroscopy, Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC Gut Decarboxylation & Oral vs. Jejunal Levodopa-Carbidopa Gel Kinetics
episodes.notes: Mechanical and microbial bottlenecks along levodopa's route from mouth to brain: videofluoroscopic discovery of tablet retention in the valleculae (Sato et al. 2018), carbidopa-insensitive gut microbial tyrosine decarboxylase (Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC) and Eggerthella lenta dopamine dehydroxylase (Maini Rekdal et al. 2019; van Kessel et al. 2019), and oral vs. continuous jejunal infusion pharmacokinetics (Othman et al. 2015).

episodes.label: The Blood That Would Not Turn Red — Acquired Methemoglobinemia (SpO2 86% vs. PaO2 85 mmHg), Multi-Wavelength Co-Oximetry, NADPH Reductase & G6PD Methylene Blue Hemolysis
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Pharmacology deep dive into acquired methemoglobinemia and antidote mechanics: why dual-wavelength pulse oximetry locks near 85–86% despite high dissolved arterial PaO2, multi-wavelength co-oximetry separation of ferric (Fe3+) methemoglobin, how methylene blue uses NADPH methemoglobin reductase as an artificial electron shuttle, and why G6PD deficiency converts methylene blue into a trigger for acute Heinz-body hemolysis (Mathiyalagan et al. 2025; ProvayBlue US label).

episodes.label: The Antibiotic at the Other Ribosome — Linezolid Hyperlactatemia, Mitoribosome COX-II vs. Nuclear Tom20/SDHA Translation, Paired PBMC Recovery & Duration Cohort Denominators
episodes.notes: Translational pharmacology and mitochondrial toxicology of oxazolidinone antibiotics: linezolid-associated hyperlactatemia despite 98% arterial oxygen saturation (Chaudhri et al. 2024, 4.9->5.1->1.6 mmol/L), selective depletion of mitoribosome-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits vs. nuclear-encoded Tom20 and SDHA in human HL-60/THP-1 cells (Milosevic et al. 2018), paired patient PBMC recovery (Garrabou et al. 2007, COX-II protein 16% and enzyme activity 51% of controls with intact mtDNA/mRNA), and 40-patient cross-sectional duration cohorts (Martínez-Guitián et al. 2026).

episodes.label: The Signal That Outlasted the Cigarette — Exhaled CO vs. Urine Cotinine & Anabasine on Nicotine Patch, Langley's Receptor Concept, Human alpha4-beta2 nAChR Varenicline Cryo-EM (6UR8) & the EAGLES Trial

episodes.label: The Flush That Fooled the Numbers — Extended-Release Niacin vs. Nicotinamide, Goldberger's Pellagra, HCAR2/GPR109A Cryo-EM (8IJA), Langerhans PGD2/DP1 Flushing & AIM-HIGH/HPS2-THRIVE Trial Futility
episodes.notes: From pellagra prevention to the HDL surrogate fallacy: nicotinic acid vs. nicotinamide chemistry, human HCAR2/GPR109A cryo-EM structure bound to niacin (PDB 8IJA), Langerhans-cell and keratinocyte PGD2/DP1 flushing vs. laropiprant blockade, glycine-conjugation vs. amidation metabolic saturation, and the AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE cardiovascular outcome trials.

episodes.label: The Dose That Bought Another Hour — Parkinson's Levodopa Wearing-Off Diaries, Catechol-O-Methyltransferase (COMT) Mg2+ Coordination (PDB 7XGI), Opicapone Erythrocyte Kinetics, BIPARK-I & Tolcapone Hepatotoxicity
episodes.notes: From Parkinson's wearing-off diaries to peripheral COMT inhibition: separating seated motor OFF time from orthostatic hypotension, competing AADC and COMT metabolic pathways, rat soluble COMT crystal structure bound to opicapone and Mg2+ (PDB 7XGI), plasma LC-MS/MS vs. sustained erythrocyte COMT inhibition kinetics, BIPARK-I/II trial endpoints, and tolcapone vs. opicapone hepatic safety.

episodes.notes: Evolutionary genomics and functional regulatory biology of high-altitude adaptation on the Tibetan Plateau: 89 ancient genomes spanning 5,100 years beginning at Zongri (Wang et al. 2023), Denisovan-like EPAS1 haplotype introgression and selection timing (Huerta-Sánchez et al. 2014; Zhang et al. 2021), hypoxia-responsive ENH5 enhancer reporter and deletion experiments (Gray et al. 2022), and iPSC-derived endothelial transcriptomics under hypoxia (Gray et al. 2025).

episodes.label: The Reference Sample Had Changed — Post-Transplant Forensic DNA Chimerism Across Blood (100% Donor), Buccal Swabs (Mixed Leukocyte Infiltration) & Hair/Eyebrow Follicles
episodes.notes: Forensic genetics of biological chimerism after allogeneic hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation: why blood reference samples convert completely to the donor's STR and amelogenin sex profile, why buccal swabs yield variable donor-recipient DNA mixtures due to mucosal leukocyte trafficking, and why hair shafts and eyebrow follicles remain reliable recipient reference tissues (Jacewicz et al. 2013; Li et al. 2014; 2026 eyebrow follicle study).

episodes.notes: Pulmonary diagnostics and flexible bronchoscopy (H049) for occult adult airway foreign bodies: Nguyen Phan et al.'s (2026) two-year missed sapodilla seed aspiration masquerading as recurrent right-lower-lobe pneumonia and asthma, radiolucent organic foreign-body CT physics, granulation-tissue tumor mimics, and flexible vs. rigid bronchoscopic retrieval across adult cohorts (Jang et al. 2022; Purohit et al. 2023).

episodes.label: The Movement After the Missing Breath — Video-Polysomnography (H044), Obstructive Sleep Apnea Arousal Pseudo-RBD vs. True REM Sleep Without Atonia & CPAP Resolution
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain Diagnostics (H044) investigation of nocturnal dream-enactment mimics: how synchronized video-polysomnography (EEG, EOG, submental/limb EMG, nasal pressure, and thoracoabdominal effort belts) separates true alpha-synucleinopathy REM sleep behavior disorder (sustained/phasic REM sleep without atonia) from severe obstructive sleep apnea respiratory-arousal pseudo-RBD that resolves completely on CPAP (Deguchi et al. 2021; Bergmann et al. 2024).

episodes.label: The Breath the Spirometer Missed — Normal Spirometry with 31% Predicted DLCO, Plethysmographic Lung Volumes, Combined Fibrosis & Emphysema (CPFE) & ERS/ATS Standards
episodes.notes: Behind the Curtain medical testing family H043 (Lung Volumes & Diffusing Capacity): why a patient can have FVC 112% predicted and TLC 88% predicted alongside a single-breath DLCO of 31% predicted (Neder et al. 2019), how opposing mechanical effects of emphysema and pulmonary fibrosis preserve lung volumes while destroying alveolar-capillary gas transfer (Kim et al. 2022 IPF-PRO registry, N=934; Barisione et al. 2014), and the 2017 ERS/ATS single-breath CO uptake standard (Graham et al. 2017).

episodes.label: The Seconds That Grew After the Fall — Stetson & Eagleman's 31-Meter Free-Fall Flicker Experiment, Oddball Predictability & Duration vs. Passage-of-Time Judgments
episodes.notes: Experimental psychophysics of subjective time dilation and duration judgment: Stetson, Fiesta & Eagleman's (2007) 31-meter, 2.49-second free-fall experiment separating retrospective stopwatch expansion (2.96 s recalled vs. 2.17 s imagined, +36%) from unchanged wrist-LED flicker resolution, Pariyadath & Eagleman's (2007) visual oddball duration vs. pitch/flicker dissociation, and Martinelli & Droit-Volet's (2022, N=803) separation of numerical duration estimates from passage-of-time feelings.

episodes.label: How a Vitamin Can Change a Blood Test’s Result — Green's 1963 Avidin-Biotin Kinetics, Streptavidin Capture Immunoassays, Trambas Spiking/Depletion Controls & Sandwich vs. Competitive Interference
episodes.notes: Biochemical kinetics and clinical laboratory physics of biotin immunoassay interference: Green's (1963) radiotracer measurement of avidin-biotin association/exchange, Bayer & Wilchek's (1974) affinity-capture chemistry, Trambas et al.'s (2018) paired serum biotin-spiking and streptavidin-depletion reversal experiments, and Li et al.'s (2017) human supplementation crossover demonstrating opposite interference directions in sandwich vs. competitive immunoassays.

episodes.label: How a Flash Test Separates the Retina’s Responses — Adrian's 1945 Red/Blue Scotopic-Photopic ERG, Dilated-Pupil Control, Miyake's Electronegative CSNB Waveform & ISCEV Standards
episodes.notes: Retinal electrophysiology and clinical waveform dissection: Edgar Adrian's (1945) human corneal-thread ERG separating scotopic and photopic responses across wavelengths with dilated-pupil controls, Miyake et al.'s (1986, N=64) electronegative bright-flash ERG in congenital stationary night blindness (preserved photoreceptor a-wave with reduced ON-bipolar b-wave), and 2022 ISCEV full-field and On-Off ERG standards.

episodes.label: How Pancreas Tests Separate Secretion from Sample Dilution — Burton's 1960 Secretin-Pancreozymin Challenge, Endoscopic Bicarbonate Crossover, Stool Elastase & Lyophilized Water Correction
episodes.notes: Gastrointestinal physiology and specimen physics of exocrine pancreatic testing: from Bayliss & Starling's (1902) secretin discovery and Burton et al.'s (1960) duodenal secretin-pancreozymin aspiration to endoscopic vs. tube bicarbonate crossover validation (Stevens et al. 2006), fecal elastase immunoassay validation (Löser et al. 1996), and Fischer et al.'s (2001) paired freeze-drying experiment showing 16/151 diarrheal stool samples normalize once corrected for water dilution.

episodes.label: How B12 Testing Separates Supply from Absorption — Castle's 1929 Intrinsic Factor Experiment, Schilling's 1953 Two-Stage Radiotracer Assay, Methylmalonic Acid & Anti-IF Antibodies
episodes.notes: Hematologic and biochemical physiology of vitamin B12 diagnostics: Castle's (1929) sequential extrinsic-plus-intrinsic factor reticulocyte experiments, Schilling's (1953) two-stage radiolabeled urinary absorption test with and without intrinsic factor replacement, and modern three-axis serum cobalamin, methylmalonic acid (MMA), and intrinsic-factor antibody testing.

episodes.label: How a Blood Test Keeps a History of Glucose — Rahbar's 1968 Diabetic Hemoglobin Fraction, Bunn's 1976 59Fe-Transferrin Glycation Kinetics, Red-Cell Age & the ADAG Trial
episodes.notes: Biochemistry and hematologic kinetics of glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c): Rahbar's (1968) discovery in diabetic erythrocytes, Bunn et al.'s (1976) 59Fe-transferrin pulse-chase proof of slow non-enzymatic postsynthetic Amadori glycation, Fitzgibbons et al.'s (1976) density-fraction proof of erythrocyte age dependence, and Nathan et al.'s (2008) ADAG calibration.

episodes.label: What an Ear Test Learns by Changing the Pressure — Terkildsen & Thomsen's 1959 Pressure Sweep, Jerger's 1970 Type A/B/C Curves, Equivalent Canal Volume & Infant 1,000 Hz Probes
episodes.notes: Acoustic immittance physics and developmental biomechanics of tympanometry: Terkildsen & Thomsen's (1959) ear-canal pressure-sweep compliance peak, Jerger's (1970) Type A/B/C diagnostic classification, Mehta et al.'s (2006) equivalent ear-canal volume (Vec) three-way disambiguation of flat Type B traces, and Gellrich et al.'s (2024) myringotomy-validated proof of 1,000 Hz vs. 226 Hz probe tones in young infants.

episodes.label: How an Eye Scan Finds Layers with Light — Fercher's 1988 Low-Coherence Eye-Length Interferometry, Huang & Fujimoto's 1991 Retinal OCT & Preperimetric Glaucoma RNFL Loss
episodes.notes: Optical physics and clinical translation of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT): why femtosecond light propagation requires interferometric path-length matching rather than direct electronic clock timing, Fercher et al.'s (1988) low-coherence axial eye-length interferometry, Huang, Swanson & Fujimoto's (1991) cross-sectional retinal OCT invention, and Miki et al.'s (2014) longitudinal proof of structural RNFL thinning preceding visual field defects in glaucoma.

episodes.label: Why a Pulse Oximeter Needs a Pulse — Millikan & Wood's Bloodless Ear Zero, Takuo Aoyagi's 1974 Pulsatile AC/DC Ratio, Dyshemoglobin 85% Artifacts & Skin-Pigment Bias
episodes.notes: Optical physics and physiological limitations of pulse oximetry: Millikan (1942) and Wood & Geraci's (1949) pneumatic bloodless-ear zeroing, Takuo Aoyagi's (1974) breakthrough using pulsatile arterial AC/DC absorbance ratios at two wavelengths, two-wavelength degrees-of-freedom failure in carboxyhemoglobinemia and methemoglobinemia, and melanin/low-saturation occult hypoxemia bias (Bickler et al. 2005; Sjoding et al. 2020).

episodes.label: How a Test Maps Vision Away from Where You're Looking — Goldmann's 1945 Hemispherical Kinetic Bowl, Heijl & Krakau's 1975 Automated Blind-Spot Fixation & 20/20 Chiasmal Hemianopia
episodes.notes: Psychophysics and neuro-ophthalmic anatomy of visual field perimetry: Goldmann's (1945) standardized luminance hemispherical bowl and kinetic target-velocity reaction-time artifact, Heijl & Krakau's (1975) automated computerized static threshold perimetry and blind-spot catch trials, and Ogra et al.'s (2014) proof that optic chiasm compression routinely produces bitemporal visual field loss despite 6/6 (20/20) foveal acuity.
